rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation is in instance_norm_forward_kernel (non-affine). Model default: affine=True. Dispatch: if(weight.defined() && bias.defined()) uses affine kernel. Since affine=True, weight and bias are always defined nn.Parameters, so dispatch always selects instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine (unmutated). The mutated kernel at line 37 is never executed.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the loop bound from `i < spatial_size` to `i <= spatial_size` in the non-affine kernel (`instance_norm_forward_kernel`). However, the `InstanceNorm2dCustom` class defaults to `affine=True`, which creates `weight` and `bias` parameters. The CUDA dispatch logic checks `if (weight.defined() && bias.defined())` and routes to `instance_norm_forward_kernel_with_affine` when both are defined. Since the default configuration always has affine parameters, the mutated non-affine kernel is never called. This is a dead code path under the current configuration, not a value-sensitivity issue.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under value-only testing. Would require setting affine=False in InstanceNorm2dCustom constructor, which is a configuration change outside the main contract. With affine=False, the bug would manifest as thread 0 reading out-of-bounds memory (index spatial_size) in the mean calculation, corrupting normalization results.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should generate mutants only in code paths reachable under the test configuration. Alternatively, ensure test suites exercise all constructor parameter combinations (affine=True and affine=False) to achieve full branch coverage in kernel dispatch logic.
